newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end lower eyeing FOMC, mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end lower eyeing FOMC, mini-budget.

text.p: Italian stocks ended weaker in modest volume on Monday after spending most of the afternoon hovering just above session lows with operators adopting a wait and see attitude ahead of Tuesday's Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC) and details of Italy's deficit-cutting mini-budget due later this week. Easier bond futures also depressed sentiment.
"There's simply not much buying interest. The market made a timid attempt to pick itself up this afternoon, but to no avail," one dealer said.
The all-share Mibtel index ended 1.25 percent down at 11,647 and the Mib30 blue chip index 1.54 percent down at 17,167.
Food group Parmalat was an outstanding performer, putting on 7.93 percent to 2,340 lire as the market welcomed its acquisition of a majority stake in Canada's Beatrice Foods.
Insurance and financial services group Mediolanum gained 4.02 percent to 15,020 lire after Goldman Sachs began coverage of the stock with a "trading buy."
Insurer Generali rose 1.03 percent to 29,200 lire after Goldman Sachs raised the group to "market outperformer" from "market performer."
But energy group ENI lost 2.16 percent to 8,305, Olivetti slipped 1.63 percent to 609 and Pirelli E C shed 2.9 percent to 2,375 lire.
Telecoms were all easier with holding company Stet off 1.97 percent to 7,205 and Telecom Italia down 1.49 percent to 4,110.
Financial holding Gemina was suspended limit down for most of the session.
Banks were weaker with Ambroveneto off 3.23 percent to 3,810 lire and Banca di Roma down 3.2 percent at 1,118.
